title: Dissolution of a company: record of non-conciliation delivered before filing

expect.why: Company disputes, dissolution and liquidation go to the specialised commercial court ([cpca 536 مكرر ¶3]); the petition must be filed 'مرفقة ... بمحضر عدم الصلح' on pain of inadmissibility. The record was delivered five days before the petition, so it can be attached: step done.

title: Dissolution of a company: no record of non-conciliation, no exemption in the texts

expect.why: 'ترفع الدعوى ... مرفقة، تحت طائلة عدم قبول الدعوى شكلا، بمحضر عدم الصلح': the record is required and the texts given state no exemption. Step missing.

title: Dissolution of a company: the lawyer does not know whether a record exists

expect.why: The step is required before this petition (the sanction is inadmissibility) and whether it was done is unknown: a missing fact is not a no, so the rule must ask.

title: Dissolution of a company: record delivered the day after the petition date

expect.why: The text says the petition is filed 'مرفقة ... بمحضر عدم الصلح': the record must exist and accompany the petition. A record delivered after the petition date (2026-06-16 against 2026-06-15) cannot have been attached. The starting event is the delivery of the record, not the date of the conciliation session; a nearby date (the session) would wrongly give 'done'. The text does not say in so many words that delivery must precede filing; this is the natural reading of 'مرفقة'.

title: Dissolution of a company: record delivered on the day of the petition

expect.why: Delivered on the same day as the petition: it can still be attached to it, and nothing in the text requires an earlier day. Step done (edge: the delivery date equals the petition date).

title: Dissolution of a company: record said to exist, delivery date not known

expect.why: The step is only complete if the record is attached to the petition, which depends on the date it was delivered. That date is unknown (absent), so the rule must ask for it rather than say the step is done.

title: Dissolution of a company goes to the specialised commercial court

expect.why: 'تختص المحكمة التجارية المتخصصة بالنظر في ... منازعات الشركات التجارية، لا سيما منازعات الشركاء وحل وتصفية الشركات': a request for dissolution leaves the ordinary court's commercial section ([cpca 531 ¶1] excepts what [cpca 536 مكرر] lists).

title: Divorce: no record of non-conciliation is a prior step of the petition

expect.why: In divorce the conciliation attempts are compulsory ('محاولات الصلح وجوبية') but take place before the judge of the family section after the petition is filed ([cpca 436 ¶1], [cpca 440 ¶1]); the text asks for no record with the petition. The record-with-the-petition rule is that of the specialised commercial court only. A rule that blocks this petition for lack of a record is wrong: no step is required before filing.

title: Custody and maintenance: no record of non-conciliation is required

expect.why: Maintenance and custody claims belong to the family section ('دعاوى النفقة والحضانة وحق الزيارة'); none of the texts given requires a record of non-conciliation before filing them. Not done and no step is required.

title: Wages claim against an employer in bankruptcy or judicial settlement

expect.why: [cpca 500 ¶2] gives the social section exclusive jurisdiction over the performance of employment contracts; [cpca 536 مكرر ¶4] gives the specialised commercial court 'التسوية القضائية والإفلاس'. The texts given do not say which governs a wage claim against a bankrupt employer: the text does not settle this, the rule must warn, not decide.

title: Wages claim against an employer: bankruptcy status not known

expect.why: Whether the case may leave the social section turns on the employer's bankruptcy or settlement, which is unknown: ask the lawyer.

title: Wages claim by a civil servant or an agent under the public statute

expect.why: [cpca 500 ¶2] covers contracts of employment; the texts given say nothing of civil servants or of the administrative courts, so they do not settle whether this claim stays with the social section. The text does not settle this; the rule must warn, not decide.

title: Rescission claim where a party is a public administrative body

expect.why: The court has general jurisdiction over civil, commercial and other cases ([cpca 32 ¶3]); the texts given contain no rule that sends cases involving a public administrative body elsewhere. The texts do not settle it: warn, never decide. (The contrasting party, a public company, would not be an exit on these texts either.)
